proposed.why: No tool calls are left. The evidence shows the provider stopped answering, which opened the breaker, and this caused the 503s and the latency.

diagnosis.hypothesis: Starting about 19:01, fake-provider (standing in for the outside payment company) stopped answering payments-api's calls to /v1/payments and /v1/refunds in time, so those calls ended in client ReadTimeouts. The timed-out calls held each POST /payments open for seconds, which pushed p95 to 4.8 s. The run of failures tripped payments-api's circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on). With the breaker open, payments-api answers new payments with 503 and leaves them pending, so the 5xx share rose to about 90%. The breaker is working as designed: it fails fast and protects us. The trigger is outside our services. No deploy stands out: every container was created together at 18:59:27, the settings look normal, and every container is healthy. Still open: why the provider went slow. Its container reports healthy, and we cannot see inside it. It may be an injected provider outage or slowness.

evidence.shows: POST /payments 503s rose from ~0.04/s to 9.5/s at 19:01:13–19:01:43, while 201s fell from ~3/s to 0.16/s.

Provider attempts to /v1/payments and /v1/refunds started ending in ReadTimeout (no_answer) from 19:01:03 at ~1.5/s, while 200 answers collapsed toward 0. Some 500s were also present at a low steady rate (~0.1–0.24/s).
payments-api ERROR logs: 'provider unavailable; payment left pending', with the error '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open'. The breaker is open and short-circuiting calls.
Completed provider HTTP calls (200 and 500 responses) dropped to near zero by 19:01:48. The timeouts do not appear here as responses.
Provider calls that did complete were fast (p95 ~5 ms). So the latency comes from calls that got no answer and timed out, not from slow answers.
All services were deployed at the same moment, 18:59:27, with normal-looking settings (breaker on, cents, idempotent ledger). No recent change in our services lines up with 19:01.
All containers, fake-provider included, are running and healthy with 0 restarts. The provider is up but not answering in time.

proposed_fix.summary: Do not roll back anything: none of our deploys caused this, and the breaker is limiting the damage. Escalate to the provider (check its status) and keep the breaker on. Once the provider answers again, the breaker's trial calls will close it. Then reconcile the payments left pending during the outage: run the money check, and retry or resolve the pending payments idempotently. Watch klaxon_payments_pending and the ReadTimeout rate.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No action is taken now. While the provider is out, new payments and refunds keep failing with 503 and pile up as pending. Customers see failures until the provider recovers.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo, since no change is made. If later reconciliation of the pending payments goes wrong, stop it and restore from the idempotency keys and the provider's records.
